title: Research vocabulary map
description: The search protocol for a published-user-research survey, built BEFORE any searching. Four axes, typed expansions with honest provenance, per-angle applicability verdicts, and the wave-0 source posture.

short_reason.description: Required when the group carries fewer than three expansions. A thin group is an honest result for a narrow term; padding it manufactures queries that return noise.

negative_terms.description: Exclusion terms. Required on `method` groups: method vocabulary collides hard with ordinary language and with other disciplines — 'diary study', 'card sort' and 'interview' all retrieve enormous amounts of unrelated literature, and a query built from such a group cannot be made precise afterwards.

provenance.description: `extracted` claims a real corpus supplied this term and requires that you actually looked. The map is built BEFORE the search, so unless a probe ran, the honest value is `model-knowledge` — which a reviewer weighs differently rather than rejecting.

relation.description: SKOS relation to the canonical term.

absent_types.description: An axis carrying no group must appear here with a reason. An axis neither present nor declared silently empties every angle that depends on it.

precondition.description: The registry's precondition, verbatim. Restating it in your own words is where a verdict quietly stops matching the predicate it claims to evaluate.

reason.description: Grounded in the scope's actual values, not a general impression.

release.description: The version or wave read, or the literal 'rolling' for a continuously-updated source with no release concept.

active.description: A source is `active` only if you reached it at wave 0. Every later angle's applicable set is intersected with this list, so a source left in `skipped` is a source no angle can query.

inferred_from.description: The SIGNAL the assumption rests on, not the rationale for wanting it.

group_type.description: The four axes a research search queries from. `user-population` names who was studied; `task` names what they were doing; `method` names the study designs whose vocabulary retrieves this literature at all; `component` names widget terms, because assistive-technology research is indexed by widget rather than by task alone.

access_status.description: How this source was reachable AT as_of. Deliberately NOT the same field or the same values as the sibling surveys' `access` — this enum grades RETRIEVABILITY OF FULL TEXT, which is the axis this survey's admission rule turns on. `paywalled-abstract-only` is the load-bearing member: it is a fetch success that still cannot support a record, because a finding extracted from an abstract is indistinguishable from one grounded in the method section. `throttled` means the source answered AT LEAST ONCE and rate-limits — reachable, so it belongs in `sources.active`, and its later refusals are `rate-limited` cells. A source that refused every wave-0 attempt was never established as reachable and belongs in `sources.skipped` as `blocked`. Without `throttled`, a source that answers intermittently has no posture: grading it `blocked` forces it into `skipped` where no angle may query it, and the cell-level `rate-limited` status becomes unreachable by construction. `crawl-delayed` is a delay the source DECLARES up front; `throttled` is one it applies under load.

status.description: `not-fetched` is for a posture established WITHOUT retrieving content — there was nothing to sanitize. `unavailable` says the different thing that sanitization was attempted and degraded, so using it here misreports what happened.

cause.description: Required unless status is sanitized: what was degraded, or what triggered the withholding.
